podcast.body: Although the third album in Bowie's "Berlin trilogy," it was recorded in Switzerland and New York, yet maintained the stylistic feel of his German period with Brian Eno contributing (Tony Visconti produced). Initially the least commercially successful of the three and puzzling to critics and fans upon its spring 1979 release, it has since been re-evaluated as an underrated, artsy, and experimental album, anticipating new wave and post-punk music. "Lager was the least commercially successful of these three albums."

podcast.body: As part of a trilogy of albums made in Berlin, "Lodger" was created by Bowie after he was profoundly inspired by early Krautrock and Kraftwerk. These works represent a pivotal, fascinating period in his career. "They was low, they were heroes, and larger."

podcast.body: Recorded in Switzerland with final touches in the United States, this album was created during a break in the *Heroes* tour. Robert Fripp was not involved; Adrian Belew (a future King Crimson member) took his place. Brian Eno's Oblique Strategies were crucial, inspiring ideas like playing old Bowie melodies backward and musicians swapping instruments to foster spontaneity. The album abandoned the electronic and ambient sound of *Low* and *Heroes* for more conventional songs, combining New Wave, World Music, pop, and Krautrock influences. While there were no arguments during recording, the creative spark between Bowie and Eno from their previous two albums seemed to be fading. "El disco abandonó el lado más electrónico y ambiental de sus dos anteleles trabajos a favor de canciones más convencionales, por decirlo de alguna manera."

podcast.body: Recorded starting in mid-1978, this album is described as the most complicated, controversial, and doubt-inducing of the Berlin Trilogy. It was not recorded in Berlin but in the United States, Switzerland, and some parts in Paris. Critical reception was mixed; it was often misunderstood, didn't receive excellent reviews, and was seen as the weakest of the trilogy upon release, with some critics not even considering it part of the trilogy. It features significant influences from World Music and Brian Eno, but fewer Krautrock and German music influences than previous albums, lacking their complex instrumental parts. Despite initial reception, *Lodger* gained significant charisma, followers, and fans over the years, becoming a point of inflection in the early 1990s as it contained the "germ" of much of Bowie's sound in the 1980s and 1990s. "Lodger que además, pues, es un disco complicado, es un disco complejo, a veces es un tanto polémico."

podcast.body: Released in the spring of 1979, this album reached number 20 on the Billboard album chart. It was mostly not recorded in Berlin, but rather tracked in Montrose, Switzerland, and New York City. The album employed the same Eno-centric recording techniques as "Low" and "Heroes," though it was characterized as less like Art Rock and more like quirky new wave pop. "Released in the spring of 1979, Lager reached number 20 on the Billboard album chart and spun off a couple of minor hit singles."
